reviewNote: Draft transcribed from the one-page illustrated sheet (QJ8782). Part letters and step order must be confirmed by the factory before this is served to customers as authoritative guidance.

steps.title: Bolt the base and lower board
steps.detail: Drive the B fittings into the base plate D from underneath, lay the lower hideout board E on top, and drive the A screws with the C Allen key. The sheet notes that spare screws may remain.

steps.title: Stand the four 40 cm columns
steps.detail: Stand four P1 (40 cm) columns upright on the base plate and fasten each from below with an A screw.

steps.title: Lock the first deck
steps.detail: Seat board E onto the four P1 columns, tighten the B fittings, and prepare the P5 posts for the next level.

steps.title: Build the hideout box
steps.detail: Assemble the hideout from the front F, right G, left H, rear I and top J boards, fitting the K, L and M spaceship decks and the N observatory into the openings as shown on the sheet.

steps.title: Raise the hideout level
steps.detail: Fit two P2 (50 cm) columns onto the hideout top and lock them with B fittings.

steps.title: Mount the middle platform
steps.detail: Add the P3 (20 cm) and P1 columns that carry the middle platform, securing the deck with A screws and B fittings.

steps.title: Fit the top deck
steps.detail: Finish with board K and two P2 columns on the upper level, then check every fitting is snug before lifting the tower upright.

safety: Build the tower on the floor with two people, then lift it upright together — a 73 in tower is awkward to raise alone.
Tighten fittings by hand until snug; overtightening crushes the birch veneer and weakens the joint.
Fix the anti-topple strap to a wall stud before the first cat uses the tower.
Re-check all A and B fittings after the first week of use, then every few months.
Replace any sisal sleeve that has worn through to the core column instead of rewinding it.
